title: The Stripe Compressor Meets Confetti
premise: A messenger wants to shrink an image description, but a repeated-run code that helps stripes grows bulky on alternating pixels. Comparing encoded lengths reveals when this particular compression scheme helps.
hook: Can the same shortcut make one picture bigger?
visible_action: Long same-color strips become count-color tokens; alternating pixels produce many small tokens and a longer ruler.
intended_takeaway_or_theme: Compression effectiveness depends on both the data and the encoding overhead.
gate: Specify token costs and a reversible toy encoding; avoid claims about all compression.

editorial_pick.original_reason: Compressible stripes and noisy confetti make the difference in repeated structure visible.
editorial_pick.proposed_first_version: Show the same encoding rule applied to two small patterns. Keep a compact symbol count beside the action.
editorial_pick.gate: State the exact simplified encoding. Verify counts and avoid claiming all real compressors behave identically.
